settings.label: Secret API key (v2)
settings.meaning: Reads the project's customers, their entitlements, subscriptions and purchases, and its offerings and products; grants and revokes promotional entitlements; deletes customers. Server only.
settings.whereToFind: Project settings › API keys › + New secret API key, version V2. Give it customer_information:customers:read_write, customer_information:subscriptions:read, customer_information:purchases:read, and project_configuration:entitlements:read, offerings:read, packages:read and products:read. Keys start with sk_. RevenueCat has no test keys: sandbox purchases are marked sandbox in the same project.

settings.label: Project ID
settings.meaning: The project every v2 call is made in. The secret key must belong to it.
settings.whereToFind: Project settings › General › Project ID (it looks like proj1ab2c3d4).

settings.label: Public SDK key (Apple)
settings.meaning: Configures the RevenueCat SDK in the app's iOS and macOS clients. The server never uses it; it's here so a host hands it to the clients.
settings.whereToFind: Project settings › API keys, the App Store app's public SDK key (also under Apps › the app). In debug builds you may use the Test Store key instead; never ship it in a release build.

settings.label: Public SDK key (Android)
settings.meaning: Configures the RevenueCat SDK in the app's Android client. The server never uses it.
settings.whereToFind: Project settings › API keys, the Play Store app's public SDK key (also under Apps › the app). In debug builds you may use the Test Store key instead; never ship it in a release build.

settings.label: Public SDK key (web)
settings.meaning: Configures the RevenueCat web SDK in the app's browser client. The server never uses it.
settings.whereToFind: Project settings › API keys, the web app's public SDK key (also under Apps › the app).

settings.label: Webhook authorization header
settings.meaning: The Authorization header value RevenueCat sends with every webhook, checked on each delivery. You choose it.
settings.whereToFind: A long random string of your own, entered as the authorization header in Integrations › Webhooks › the webhook's configuration.

settings.label: Webhook signing secret
settings.meaning: Checks the HMAC signature RevenueCat puts on each webhook, when HMAC signing is turned on. Preferred over the header alone: it covers the body and a timestamp.
settings.whereToFind: Integrations › Webhooks › the webhook › turn on HMAC webhook signing, and copy the secret: it's shown once. Rotate secret replaces it at once.

operations.name: customers.get
operations.purpose: Reads a customer by its App User ID, with its active entitlements.

operations.name: customers.delete
operations.purpose: Permanently deletes a customer. RevenueCat queues the deletion; a later get answers 404 once it's done.

operations.name: customers.grantEntitlement
operations.purpose: Grants a promotional entitlement until a time. A grant whose expiry is within two hours of an existing grant's is ignored, so a retry is harmless.

operations.name: customers.revokeGrantedEntitlement
operations.purpose: Revokes every active promotional grant of an entitlement; access ends at once. Store purchases are untouched.

operations.name: activeEntitlements.list
operations.purpose: Lists a customer's active entitlements, a page at a time.

operations.name: subscriptions.list
operations.purpose: Lists a customer's subscriptions in every store, a page at a time, optionally only sandbox or production.

operations.name: purchases.list
operations.purpose: Lists a customer's one-time purchases, a page at a time, optionally only sandbox or production.

operations.name: entitlements.list
operations.purpose: Lists the project's entitlements, each with its id (entl…) and its lookup key.

operations.name: offerings.list
operations.purpose: Lists the project's offerings, with their packages and products, for a paywall.

operations.name: products.list
operations.purpose: Lists the project's products, optionally of one app.

signature.description: With HMAC signing on, the header is t=<Unix seconds>,v1=<hex>, where v1 is the hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" keyed with the signing secret, compared in constant time; reject a t more than five minutes from now. RevenueCat recomputes t and v1 on every retry. Without it (or as well), the Authorization header carries the value set in the dashboard (webhookAuthorization), compared in constant time. The body is { api_version, event }; event.id is the same on every retry: dedupe on it.

events.meaning: A test event sent from the dashboard.
A new subscription was purchased.
A subscription renewed, or a lapsed customer subscribed again.
A subscription or non-renewing purchase was cancelled or refunded. Access lasts until EXPIRATION.
A cancelled subscription that hadn't expired was turned back on.
A purchase that won't renew.
A subscription will pause at the end of its period.
A subscription expired: access ends.
A charge failed; the subscription may still be in a grace period.
The customer changed the subscription's product.
The current period's end was pushed back.
A refund was reversed.
An unpaid invoice was issued for a RevenueCat Billing purchase.
Purchases and entitlements moved between App User IDs (transferred_from, transferred_to).
Short access (at most 24 hours) while a store couldn't validate a purchase.
A virtual currency balance changed.
The customer was enrolled in an experiment.
A web purchase was redeemed and linked to an App User ID.
A price increase needs the customer's consent before the next renewal.
The customer consented to a price increase.
Deprecated: a new App User ID was linked to an existing customer.
